clue.text: Complain about partners being put under spell

indicators.note: one word placed about another goes around it, so the complaint wraps the partners

parts.note: to bitch is slang for to complain
West and East are partners at the bridge table, giving W and E

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles because their partners have been bewitched.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, W and E (West and East) play as partners against N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewitch is to cast a spell over someone, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Order member to be concerned about right

indicators.note: the worrying word goes around the letter for right

parts.note: to bother is to take trouble or be concerned

explanation.surface: A member of a religious order frets about doing the right thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother is a man belonging to a religious order such as monks or friars.

clue.text: What's left inside we had forcibly seized

indicators.note: the remainder sits within the contraction

parts.note: we'd is the contraction of we had
the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: The remainder was grabbed by force from within our group.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrested means taken away by violent pulling or struggle.

clue.text: Train from Waterloo heading North, crossing West End

indicators.note: the reversed word crosses over, holding the letter inside it
in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: Napoleon's defeat at Waterloo was a rout, a crushing defeat

indicators.note: end of a word means its last letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the word west

explanation.surface: A train leaves Waterloo station heading north through London's West End.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo is a London station and the West End is its theatre district; here Waterloo means a decisive defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor someone is to train or teach them individually.

clue.text: Source of beer and whisky, that's enjoyed by young players

parts.note: hops are the plant that flavours beer
Scotch is whisky from Scotland

explanation.surface: Beer and whisky enjoyed by young players, a mildly scandalous picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a playground game of hopping through numbered squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: Talk together about island as source of timber

indicators.note: the talk goes around the island, so the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: to confer is to discuss together

explanation.surface: People discuss an island as a place to source wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer is a cone-bearing tree such as pine, widely grown for softwood lumber.

clue.text: Penetrated one's skin

parts.note: cut means pierced or penetrated
one's read as 'one is', with one as I and the 's as S, giving IS

explanation.surface: Something has pierced someone's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical term for the skin, the dermis plus epidermis.

clue.text: Calm, never flustered? Not so

indicators.note: flustered means thrown into confusion, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: less means not so much

explanation.surface: Was the person calm and never flustered? Not quite.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerveless means cool and composed, showing no nervousness.

clue.text: African plant is set up in liberated area

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: free means liberated

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means read upwards, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: An African plant is placed in a freed area.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering plant native to southern Africa.

clue.text: It isn't common as reward for writer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a payment to an author per copy sold

explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' means commoners, people who are not royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalty means kings and queens, and also an author's fee for each sale of their book.

clue.text: Excel in eminence in public work

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone rises to prominence through their public service.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise higher than, surpassing others in height or rank.

clue.text: Restyle, originally, in short fashion

indicators.note: the answer was originally the word restyle before its letters were moved, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A note on restyling something, delivered briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's letters are those of restyle in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tersely means briefly and curtly, so in a short manner.

clue.text: Multiple goals, perhaps, represented in kitsch art

indicators.note: re-presented, these letters are set out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Footballers scoring several goals are depicted in tacky artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat-trick is three goals by one player; 'perhaps' allows that the term also covers wickets or wins.

clue.text: Moderate line that supports creative effort

parts.note: to ease something is to moderate or lessen it

explanation.surface: A gentle line of thought that underpins creative work.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the stand that holds an artist's canvas while painting.

clue.text: It detects vehicle approaching in either direction

definitions.text: It detects vehicle approaching in either direction

parts.words: It detects vehicle approaching in either direction
parts.note: a device that spots cars coming, and itself a word that reads the same either way

explanation.surface: A device that picks up a car coming from either way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the device, with a nod to its spelling reading the same forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar locates approaching objects by bouncing radio waves off them, as in police speed traps.

clue.text: Loutish group of players getting plastered

parts.note: rough means coarse and loutish
a cast is the group of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A rowdy theatre troupe getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' suggests drunk, but here it means coated with plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughcast describes a wall coated with a coarse plaster of lime and gravel.

clue.text: Part of Ireland far away, going by air

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a county in the Republic of Ireland
second meaning: the place that is 'a long way' in the famous song, an air being a tune

explanation.walkthrough: 'Going by air' suggests a flight; air here means a tune, the wartime song 'It's a Long Way to Tipperary'.
explanation.definitionFit: The county is famous from the First World War marching song about its great distance.

clue.text: Assigned task to catch up Dr Jekyll, for example?

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading upwards, so both pieces are reversed

parts.note: a remit is the task or area of responsibility given to someone
to trap is to catch

explanation.surface: Someone is given the job of catching up with Dr Jekyll.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Jekyll is only Jekyll some of the time; the rest he is Mr Hyde.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-timer works only some hours, as Jekyll is himself only part of the time.

clue.text: Clerk shut up drug offender

parts.note: to pen is to confine or shut up
a pusher is someone who sells illegal drugs

explanation.surface: An office worker locked away a dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is a disparaging term for an office worker doing routine paperwork.

clue.text: Occur after end overturned in unexpected hazard

indicators.note: the word for occur comes after the reversed piece
turned over in a down clue, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: a tip is an end
to fall, as in a date falling on Monday, is to occur

explanation.surface: Something turns up after an end is flipped over, an unforeseen danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden danger or difficulty, originally a concealed pit as a trap.

clue.text: Getting closer to eccentric grannie

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, out of the usual order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Approaching a quirky grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearing means approaching, coming closer to something.

clue.text: Starts to prepare Wimbledon courts for top players?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: grass ..., the start of the lawns at Wimbledon
second meaning: seeded players, ranked highest in a tournament draw

explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the grass-court tennis championship, so its courts begin as grass sown from seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeds are both what grass grows from and the ranked players kept apart in a tournament draw.

clue.text: Stone used in English edifice, or construction of St Paul's

indicators.note: the stone is used inside the building, so it goes within

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building
st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: Stone used in an English building, or in building St Paul's Cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'St Paul's' suggests the London cathedral, but it means the apostle Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul composed many epistles, the letters of the New Testament.

clue.text: Amount woman combined in account, in short

indicators.note: combined means the two pieces are joined together

parts.note: a sum is an amount
Mary is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A sum and a woman added together in a ledger, briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary is a brief account giving the main points.

clue.text: Refuse after short time, showing poor judgment

indicators.note: the word for poor judgment follows the abbreviated time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
rash means acting without proper thought

explanation.surface: Turning something down too quickly shows bad judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Trash is rubbish or waste, a synonym of refuse as a noun.

clue.text: Questions and answers in schematic arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of the word's letters gives a new order

explanation.surface: A Q&A laid out in diagram form.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechism is a summary of religious doctrine in question-and-answer format.

clue.text: Jump over net

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... a fence is to jump over it
second meaning: as an adjective, after deductions

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a tennis ball over the net; net is the after-tax sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear means both leaping over an obstacle and remaining after deductions, as clear profit.

clue.text: Band with little room, at first, for large instrument

indicators.note: the small room comes at first, before the band

parts.note: a cell is a small room
O is a ring, a band shape

explanation.surface: A band with a small rehearsal room, first making space for a big instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a large bowed string instrument played seated.

clue.text: Create disturbance — a barrier contains it

indicators.note: the barrier holds the following word inside it

parts.note: a gate is a barrier across an opening

explanation.surface: A barrier holds back something that causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up trouble or unrest, as a political agitator does.

clue.text: Armed citizens prepare to fire back — I fired inside

indicators.note: the second group of letters goes inside the reversed word
back means the word for aiming is read in reverse

parts.note: to aim is what one does before shooting
lit means set alight, fired

explanation.surface: Civilians in arms ready their guns and shoot in return.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a military force raised from ordinary civilians rather than professional soldiers.

clue.text: Substitute for match, less effective in scrum?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a device for making a flame instead of a match
second meaning: weighing less, so less able to push in a rugby scrum

explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitute' and 'match' suggest a sports team change; a scrum is the rugby set piece where heavier forwards push harder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarette lighter replaces matches; a lighter pack has less weight to drive the scrum.

clue.text: Man on board finishes off the repair quickly in colony

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece, a man on the chessboard

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the next words is taken

parts.note: the last letters of the, repair and quickly

explanation.surface: A chess piece hurries to repair something within a community.
